objective: Verify that the Booking API rejects reservations whose check-out date is not strictly after the check-in date, on both the create and update paths, without breaking existing reservations that already violate the rule.

scope.rationale: Confirm POST /booking and PATCH /booking/{id} enforce the date-range rule and that valid ranges still succeed.
scope.justified_by: Acceptance criteria 1 to 4 describe create and update behaviour explicitly.

scope.rationale: Exercise the boundary where checkout equals checkin, which the ticket separates from checkout before checkin.
scope.justified_by: Error contract table distinguishes DATE_RANGE_INVALID from DATE_RANGE_ZERO.

scope.rationale: Assert the 400 response body names the offending field and carries the documented error code.
scope.justified_by: Requirement: 'The error body must name the offending field.'

scope.rationale: Confirm reservations that already violate the rule are readable and updatable on unrelated fields.
scope.justified_by: Requirement: 'Existing reservations that already violate the rule must not be broken.'

scope.rationale: Measure p95 latency of the create path under the stated load to confirm validation adds no material cost.
scope.justified_by: Description states 'Perf target: p95 under 300ms at 50 rps.'

scope.rationale: Verify the booking UI date picker consumes the new error codes correctly.
scope.justified_by: Issue link: BOOK-214 blocks BOOK-230 Booking UI date picker.

items: checkout equal to checkin returns 400 DATE_RANGE_ZERO
valid range returns 201 and persists the booking
error body names the offending field
the booking is unchanged after a rejected update
changing only checkin re-validates the whole range
changing only checkout re-validates the whole range
an existing booking that violates the rule is still readable
an unrelated field on a violating booking can still be updated
dates sent as epoch millis by legacy clients

techniques: Boundary Value Analysis on the checkin/checkout pair
Equivalence Class Partitioning across valid, inverted and zero-length ranges
Decision Table for the create and update paths against each error code
Error Guessing for malformed and legacy date formats
strategy.execution_flow: Run a smoke pass over the create and update endpoints first. If smoke fails, reject the build and wait for a stable one. On a stable build, execute the designed cases across QA and pre-prod, log defects in Jira, and send an end-of-day defect status summary. Repeat until the exit criteria are met.
best_practices: Shift-left review of the error contract before execution
Exploratory session against legacy date formats
End-to-end check through the booking UI once BOOK-230 lands

deliverables: Test scenarios and cases for the date-range rule
API test collection covering create and update

entry_exit.entry: BOOK-214 acceptance criteria and error contract are available.
entry_exit.exit: Criteria understood, ambiguities on legacy date handling resolved.

entry_exit.entry: Build deployed to QA and smoke passes.
entry_exit.exit: All designed cases executed and defects logged.

entry_exit.entry: Case results and defect reports complete.
entry_exit.exit: Test Summary Report delivered and accepted.

defect_process.severity_model: Severity by data-integrity impact, priority by proximity to the 2026.9.0 release.

tools: An API client for endpoint testing
A load tool for the p95 latency check

risks.risk: Legacy clients send dates as epoch millis, which may bypass the new validation.
risks.mitigation: Add explicit cases for epoch-millis payloads and confirm the rule applies after parsing.

risks.risk: Existing bookings that violate the rule may fail on read after the change.
risks.mitigation: Seed violating records in QA before the build lands and verify read and partial-update paths.

risks.risk: BOOK-230 (UI date picker) is not ready, blocking the integration check.
risks.mitigation: Run API-level integration checks first and defer the UI pass until BOOK-230 is deployed.

assumptions.why: The description states a p95 target at 50 rps but does not define the ramp or duration.
